newsitem.title: USA: Ill treasurer holds public fund investment hearing.
newsitem.headline: Ill treasurer holds public fund investment hearing.

text.p: Illinois Treasurer Judy Baar Topinka on Monday held the first of two scheduled hearings into the safety and soundness of the investment of public funds at all governmental levels.

Topinka hopes through the hearings to develop a uniform statewide policy to guide public investments and possibly set the percentage of holdings that any public entity could invest in riskier ventures, she said following the public hearing.

The treasurer called for hearings after a number of Illinois school districts participating in investment pools faced potential losses from investments in short-term commercial paper issued by Mercury Finance Co.

John Patti, a marketing manager for New York-based Cadre Financial Services Inc., told the Topinka panel, however, that the Illinois School District Liquid Asset Fund has a diversified portfolio to minimize the risk to the school districts.
None of the schools in the fund took losses from the Mercury investment, Patti noted.

"My concern is to start looking at what is safe and what is acceptable," Topinka said. "We have seen a number of bills in the legislature which have sought to expand the investment authority of public entities, which means a lot of public money which could go into play on a very speculative, volatile basis."

Currently, investment limitations are decided with piecemeal legislation, Topinka said. The issue should be resolved with a bill, rather than on an individual basis with amendments to existing requirements in a legislative conference committee, she said.
A mandatory policy "would be very, very helpful," Topinka said. "A thoughtful process to determine what, if any, percentage of investments are to be expanded into other than traditional areas."
Sal Bianchi, executive director of the Intergovernmental Risk Management Agency, told the panel, however, that the group needs broader investment authority, not narrower limits.
The agency pool includes 68 public entities with more than $80 million in assets used to cover accident compensation claims, Bianchi noted.
Topinka plans a second public hearing on May 5.
The Illinois House has created a commission to hold legislative hearings in the summer.
Topinka has been named head of that commission, which will include four legislators and private sector individuals.
